warmup.description: Prepare hips, knees, and posterior chain for heavy compound lifting with progressive activation.
movements: Ankle mobility rocks x 10 each side

main_exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a heavy load at 8/10 effort, leaving 1-2 reps in reserve
main_exercises.form_cue: Brace core and drive through midfoot while keeping chest tall

main_exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate-heavy load with strong hamstring tension, stopping before form breaks
main_exercises.form_cue: Hinge at hips and keep bar close to legs throughout

main_exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Dumbbell)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose a challenging load that allows full depth with control
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep front knee tracking forward and torso slightly leaned over front leg

main_exercises.name: Hip Thrust (Barbell)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a load that allows a strong glute contraction with 1-2 reps in reserve
main_exercises.form_cue: Pause at the top and fully extend hips without over-arching

main_exercises.name: Leg Extension
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate load with controlled tempo, avoiding momentum
main_exercises.form_cue: Squeeze quads at the top and lower slowly

main_exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight or moderate load with full stretch and contraction
main_exercises.form_cue: Pause briefly at the top and lower under control

cooldown.description: Reduce lower body tension and support recovery after heavy lifting.
movements: Seated hamstring stretch x 30s each side
Kneeling hip flexor stretch x 30s each side
Figure 4 glute stretch x 30s each side

phase_notes.menstrual: Heavy compound lifts like squats may feel more demanding—consider reducing load or sets while maintaining good movement quality. Focus on controlled reps and longer rest periods.
phase_notes.follicular: Ideal phase to push strength—aim to increase load on squats and RDLs while maintaining strong technique. You may feel more powerful and resilient.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Take advantage of peak strength and coordination to push your heaviest sets, especially on squats and split squats. Stay mindful of knee and hip alignment.
phase_notes.early_luteal: You can still train hard, but avoid pushing to failure—keep loads challenging but controlled. Focus on consistency and strong execution across all sets.
phase_notes.late_luteal: This session may feel highly taxing—consider reducing volume or intensity while keeping structure. Prioritize stability and avoid grinding heavy reps.
